text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Federal labs to be shut down: Ottawa closing facilities that did independent tests on pharmaceuticals, food safety.
- Serb suspects caught off guard: NATO troops kill one, capture three near site of former Bosnian prison camp.
- Neanderthal not part of our family tree: DNA too dissimilar, researchers say.
- Graft is law in Wild East: In Russia's Primorsky region, corruption runs rampant and governor calls the shots.
- Ontario aims for single-wicket shopping: Streamlining would allow residents to apply for several documents without making several trips.
- Ottawa stops new borrowing: Nesbitt economists predict bond shortages, estimates sharp drop in federal deficit.
- Renaissance stock falls 9 percent on oil estimates: 'I screwed up big-time,' CEO admits.
- KWG Resources clinches deal to complete Cuban nickel mine: Says C$300 million investment should escape U.S. retaliation.
- Report on banking reform set for today: Delivery caps week chairman resigned.
- Renaissance error rattles oil shares: It was 'cold shower time' for the oils sector yesterday as the energy company admitted production will be lower than forecast.
- EU mulls attack on Canada's film policy.
- KWG near clinching big deal in Cuba.
